title: Autoscale safeguard patterns and data-sovereignty buffer for multi-zone dedicated pools
text:
Autoscale safeguard patterns and data-sovereignty buffer for multi-zone dedicated pools

description:
Goal: implement a repeatable set of autoscaling and placement safeguards that guarantee committed throughput while honoring regional data-residency constraints and enabling graceful, low-latency failover across availability zones. Deliverables: 1) a placement scoring function and 'residency buffer' that pins minimum capacity per region/tenant, 2) autoscale policy templates (guaranteed-min, soft-buffer, emergency-drain) that operators and customers can choose, 3) soft-evacuation stencils to stagger AZ drains and preserve per-tenant throughput SLAs, and 4) observability hooks and assertion checks for compliance and audit. This ticket covers architecture, prototype implementation in the fleet orchestrator, and a staged rollout to one pilot customer and internal canary fleets.

acceptance_criteria:
Placement scoring function enforces data-residency tag and reserves a configurable 'residency buffer' for each tenant in the region (min capacity in GPU-seconds).
Autoscale policy types implemented: guaranteed-min, burstable-with-buffer, soft-drain-emergency with documented thresholds.
During simulated AZ evacuation, at least 95% of committed throughput for impacted tenants is preserved via spillover to alternate AZs or prewarmed slots within 60s in 90th percentile tests.
Per-tenant audit log entry created for every placement decision and failover action with reason codes and capacity delta.
Operator console displays current residency buffer consumption, projected shortfalls, and automated recommendations to purchase temporary burst reservations.
Security review completed and privacy/regulatory checklist signed off for pilot region (EU-West).

technical_notes:
Placement score = w1*region_affinity + w2*residency_buffer_usage + w3*latency_penalty + w4*cost_override; weights configurable per project/contract.
Residency buffer model: store per-tenant min throughput in capacity units (GPU-cores * effective tokens/s) with soft and hard thresholds. Soft threshold allows short spikes with billing; hard threshold triggers emergency drain/preempt policies.
Autoscaler modes implemented as state machine: Normal -> BufferWarning -> BufferEnforced -> EmergencyDrain. State transitions driven by aggregated per-tenant telemetry windows (10s, 60s, 5m).
Evacuation strategy: staggered 30s offsets between AZ prewarm signals, progressive traffic siphon with per-tenant token pacing, and prioritized routing for customers with SLA holds.
Compatibility: orchestrator changes must run alongside existing regional-fallback rules; strategy includes backward-compatible feature flag and traffic mirror path for 2 weeks.
Metrics to add: residency_buffer_reserved, residency_buffer_used, buffer_shortfall_events, per_tenant_committed_throughput, failover_latency_90p.
Audit requirements: immutable placement event ID, timestamp, operator-or-system principal, decision reason code, and linked commit/PR id in metadata.
Security: any placement decision exposing residency metadata to other tenants is forbidden; ensure KMS-protected telemetry and RBAC on operator UI views.

implementation_plan:
Design review with Orchestrator and Infra teams to finalize scoring function and buffer schema (week 1).
Schema change: extend tenant capacity record with residency_buffer_min, buffer_mode (soft|hard) and committed_sla_id (week 1-2).
Prototype gate: implement scoring and state machine in feature-flagged orchestrator branch; add telemetry emissions (week 2-3).
Pilot integration: deploy to internal canary fleets and one low-risk EU customer with dedicated pool; run mirrored traffic tests (week 4).
Iterate on thresholds and weight tuning based on pilot results; add operator console UI panels and alert rules (week 5).
Security review and compliance sign-off, then staged rollout to EU regions, followed by NA (week 6-8).

testing_plan:
Unit tests for scoring function and state transitions with synthetic telemetry inputs.
Large-scale simulation using historical request profiles to validate buffer consumption semantics and spillover behavior.
Load test: reserve committed capacity for test tenants and initiate sudden AZ eviction; measure throughput retention and failover latency.
Chaos test: inject random orchestrator RPC failures and ensure autoscaler does not violate hard residency constraints.
Compliance test: generate placement audit logs and run the audit parser to confirm required fields and immutability.
DR runbook drill with SREs: simulate operator-triggered emergency drain and practice rollback paths.

roll_out_steps:
Feature-flagged deploy to staging, mirror live traffic for 72h to validate no regressions.
Enable for internal canary fleets (0.5% of traffic) and run full integration test-suite.
Pilot with one EU enterprise customer under controlled SLA contract; weekly review meetings and dedicated telemetry dashboard.
Progressive ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% of regional dedicated pools after meeting throughput retention and no-severity incidents at each gate.
Post-rollout: 30-day observational period with conservative autoscale thresholds; convert to default after 30 days if stable.

comments:
2025-02-19 Asha Patel: Created ticket after stakeholder sync. Initial weight proposal: [w1=0.4, w2=0.3, w3=0.2, w4=0.1].
2025-02-21 Marcus Kim: Implemented initial scoring prototype; pushing branch for early review. Observed edge-case where small tenants with high burstiness get over-reserved when residency_buffer_min is set too high.
2025-02-24 Emma Li (PM): Recommend adding billing note to documentation for soft buffer spillover — customers should be aware of short-term billing differences when buffer is used.
2025-02-26 Javier Ortega (SRE): Need a safe-throttle if the orchestrator loses visibility of an AZ; propose a maximum prewarm concurrency to avoid double-booking capacity.
2025-03-01 Security review started; flagged telemetry encryption for residency metadata, assigned to Mei Tan for follow-up.
2025-03-02 Marcus Kim: Deployed canary branch to staging and ran synthetic evacuation test. 92% throughput preserved in initial run; tuning required to reach 95% target.
